author: Arachadonic
body:
As we all know, our two only map devs Evocal and Cow resigned recently due to the amount of hate they received over decisions they made/failed to make and a lack of back end support. 

The one reason I saw repeatedly come up was people constantly asking for them to review maps. We can all imagine how naturally this would get really annoying after awhile and it's no wonder they reached their limit.

So in an effort to prevent the next map devs coming under fire like this, I am suggesting a new rule be out in place for map submissions. The rule is as follows:
  • Asking any member of staff, including Map Devs, to review or look at your map submission will result in said map being auto-denied. If this happens then the player will also be unable to submit anymore maps for 3 weeks.
This may come across as being super strict but I feel like it is needed. We do not want another incident like the current situation to occur again. Please leave opinions below.

replies.author: Polar_Express
replies.body:
Way Harsh - It is a good idea to limit the amount of contact, but you can only make it that harsh if the Map Devs also have a requirement to give feed back with in a set time frame. 

1. Player Submits the map correctly on the forums / thread with the map files, yml, etc.
2. Map dev has (x) time to review the map and provide feedback
3. If the map dev does not give feedback then the map maker should have the right to ask without getting banned.
4. If the map is denied - the user can resubmit the map the following month no more questions. If it is accepted then an ETA on entering the rotation should be given.
4.If the map maker abuses the map dev contact policy then the user is forum banned for a given time per offence. 

We are all on the same team its not Devs/Admins Vs the player base.

replies.author: Polar_Express
replies.body: You must add a time limit or there is no function. If the Map Devs do not respond how does the player know if the map was submitted correctly, if there are any issues, etc. There must be communication guidelines for both sides. Being a map dev requires accountability also, just like a server mod, they have accountability standards. It should be a requirement that when a map is submitted then a response should be given ( that also shows respect to the player base ), the amount of time the map dev has to respond should be set in a way that it limits the "stress" on the dev team, but I for one will not make another map, if i am just submitting it " to the wind" and hope someone gets back with me, or will get around to me when ever - if ever...
